1999-05-26: Al Gore begins his campaign to succeed Bill Clinton in the November 2000 presidential election, amid trailing polls and a challenge from Bill Bradley.
1999-06-16: Al Gore formally announced his candidacy for the US presidency, promising moral leadership and distancing himself from Bill Clinton.

2000-01-24: Al Gore was projected to win the Iowa Democratic caucuses with a 2:1 lead over Bill Bradley, according to a final poll.

Article discusses Al Gore’s presidential campaign, noting his qualifications and the political burden of his association with Bill Clinton.
2000-03-07: Al Gore wins all Democratic Super Tuesday contests, including a runaway victory in New York, over Bill Bradley.
2000-03-08: Al Gore and George W. Bush shifted into general election mode after decisive Super Tuesday primary victories, with Gore proposing twice-weekly televised debates and a mutual ban on TV advertising.

2000-04-27: John Prescott travels to Washington to meet Al Gore and Republican senators to support Gore's stance on global warming and the Kyoto agreement.
2000-05-20: Supporters of Vice-President Al Gore are increasingly worried that he is losing the initiative in the 2000 US presidential election to Republican rival George W. Bush, who has re-established himself in the centre ground.

2000-07-19: Al Gore has assembled a glittering cast list of Hollywood endorsements, with 17 Oscar winners donating at least $1,000 each to his presidential campaign.
2000-08-04: Al Gore plans to announce his Democratic vice-presidential running mate, aiming to recapture the initiative after the Republican convention.
2000-08-07: Al Gore selects Senator Joseph Lieberman as his running mate, a move symbolically underlining the end of the Bill Clinton era.
2000-08-08: US Vice-President and presidential candidate Al Gore announced Senator Joseph Lieberman as his running mate, making Lieberman the first Jewish candidate on a major party ticket.
2000-08-14: Al Gore presents himself at the Democrat convention in Los Angeles for the Presidential race.
2000-08-16: Al Gore arrives in Los Angeles to secure the Democratic Party's nomination and prepare for the presidential campaign with attack strategist Bob Shrum.
2000-08-17: Al Gore accepts the Democratic presidential nomination in Los Angeles, declaring "I stand here tonight as my own man."
2000-08-19: Al Gore surged into an opinion poll lead over George W. Bush following his performance at the Democratic convention, leading 48% to 42% among registered voters in a Newsweek poll and 47% to 46% among likely voters in a Gallup/CNN survey.
2000-08-20: Article discusses Al Gore as the Democratic presidential candidate facing a potential third-party challenge from Ralph Nader.
2000-08-31: George W. Bush's presidential campaign launches its first personal attack ad against Democratic rival Al Gore, mocking his character and credibility.
2000-09-12: George W. Bush's campaign withdrew a television ad after Democrats claimed it included a subliminal message attacking Al Gore, with the word "rats" flashing before "bureaucrats."
2000-10-21: Al Gore resists pressure to deploy Bill Clinton on the campaign trail in the final stretch of the presidential race.
2000-10-25: Al Gore campaigned in Tennessee and Missouri, discussing education policy at Tennessee State University and holding rallies in Jackson and Kansas City.
2000-10-26: Al Gore campaigns in his home state of Tennessee and other traditionally Democratic states as polls show a tight race with George W. Bush.
2000-10-28: The article expresses hope that Al Gore wins the upcoming US presidential election, citing his flaws but arguing George Bush would be worse.
2000-10-29: President Bill Clinton campaigned for Al Gore by urging black Americans to vote for the Democratic candidate, while the Gore camp said it intended to keep Clinton at arm's length in the main electoral battleground.
2000-11-03: The article discusses Al Gore's character and campaign in the 2000 presidential election, noting that voters see him as dull and that his campaign is in trouble, while he tries to show a softer side before polling day.
2000-11-05: Al Gore campaigns around the clock in the final days before the US presidential election, making a last push through battleground states.
2000-11-06: A Harris Interactive poll indicates Al Gore could win the presidency in the electoral college despite George W. Bush leading the national popular vote.
2000-11-07: George W. Bush visits Tennessee, Al Gore's home state, on the final day of the presidential campaign in an attempt to taunt his rival.
Al Gore is described as being neck and neck in the polls with rival George Bush in the presidential election.

Al Gore campaigns across several states on the final day before the election and is scheduled to cast his vote in Carthage, Tennessee.
2000-11-08: Al Gore wins a slender but clear majority of the popular vote, though the final outcome of the Florida recount remains unclear.

2000-11-16: Al Gore asked a Florida judge to force the state to count disputed presidential ballots being hand tallied after a deadline had passed.
2000-11-20: Democrats were divided over how much further Al Gore should pursue his post-election struggle for the White House, as Republicans threatened to fight him to the electoral college and beyond.

2000-12-04: A Florida state judge rejected Al Gore's challenge to the certified presidential election results, refusing recounts in Palm Beach and Miami-Dade counties and dealing a serious setback to Gore's hopes of preventing George W. Bush from winning.
2000-12-13: Al Gore conceded the presidential race to George W. Bush after the US Supreme Court halted Florida recounts.
2001-01-25: Al Gore announced plans to teach and write for the next few months while considering his political future.
2001-02-26: A Miami Herald review of uncounted undervotes in Miami-Dade County suggests Al Gore would have gained only 49 net votes there, leaving George Bush ahead by 140 votes in Florida even if manual recounts had proceeded.

2002-06-29: Al Gore accused the Bush administration of incompetence in the hunt for Osama bin Laden and criticized its handling of the war on terrorism.
2002-11-18: Al Gore is promoting two new books, "Joined at the Heart" and "The Spirit of Family," co-authored with his wife Tipper, as part of a carefully planned campaign amid speculation about whether he will run for president in 2004.

2003-10-01: Former US vice-president Al Gore is reportedly in talks to acquire the cable network Newsworld International from Vivendi Universal in a deal valued at $70m.
2003-12-09: Al Gore is due to endorse Howard Dean in the Democratic presidential race at a rally in Harlem.

2004-07-25: Al Gore opens the Democratic National Convention, handing on the Democratic baton to John Kerry.
2004-11-14: Al Gore and former Goldman Sachs executive David Blood launch Generation, a London-based investment firm focused on long-term sustainability, which will begin managing their own money in the new year and seek clients toward the end of the first quarter of 2005.

2006-02-05: Al Gore appears at the Sundance Film Festival in the documentary "An Inconvenient Truth," a film based on his multimedia presentation about global warming.
2006-03-06: Al Gore gave a keynote speech at America's biggest media conference in Orlando, Florida, where he urged the media industry to contribute airtime to an upcoming public service campaign on global warming.
2006-05-24: Al Gore's documentary about global warming, An Inconvenient Truth, is released in the US.
2006-05-29: Al Gore is scheduled to speak at the Guardian Hay festival at 7 pm GMT.
2006-05-30: Al Gore delivered a lecture at the Hay festival promoting his film An Inconvenient Truth and urging action on climate change, receiving a standing ovation.
2006-06-22: Former US vice-president Al Gore met with UK Chancellor Gordon Brown in London to lobby on global warming and attended a private screening of his climate change documentary An Inconvenient Truth.

2006-08-27: Al Gore said the internet could re-engage the electorate with politics on both sides of the Atlantic.
Al Gore is scheduled to deliver the Alternative MacTaggart Lecture at the MediaGuardian Edinburgh International Television Festival.
2006-09-08: Former US vice president Al Gore's film on global warming, An Inconvenient Truth, is set to be shown in cinemas worldwide after receiving rave reviews in America and Europe.
2006-09-13: An article discusses Al Gore's failure to win the 2000 US presidential election and argues that his strategy of distancing himself from Bill Clinton's achievements contributed to his defeat.
2006-09-15: The documentary An Inconvenient Truth, narrated by Al Gore, opens in British cinemas.
2006-10-05: Al Gore unveiled plans to launch a UK version of his user-generated network Current TV with the help of BSkyB.
2006-10-06: Sky announced a deal to bring Al Gore's Current TV, a channel featuring viewer-created clips, to the UK and Ireland.
2006-10-12: Al Gore, as a non-executive director of Apple, is on a committee investigating the company's backdating of share options granted between 1997 and 2002.
2007-02-11: Al Gore announces that Current TV will launch on Virgin Media in mid-March, following a similar deal with Sky in October.
2007-02-15: Al Gore announced the "Live Earth" concerts, a series of seven global concerts to raise awareness of climate change, scheduled for July 7, 2007.
2007-02-22: Al Gore was among the announced nominees for the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize, nominated for his campaign to draw attention to global warming.
2007-02-25: Al Gore and his film An Inconvenient Truth are expected to share the Academy Award.
2007-02-27: Channel 4 wins the terrestrial television rights to Al Gore's Oscar-winning documentary An Inconvenient Truth, with the film set to air in 2008.
2007-03-12: Al Gore unveils the British version of his Current TV network, a channel relying on viewer-created content.
2007-03-14: Former US Vice-President Al Gore urged the pensions industry to adopt longer-term investment goals, warning that short-termism risks undermining sustainable economies and progress on climate change.
2007-03-21: Al Gore returned to Congress to testify on global warming, receiving a positive reception.
2007-04-14: Al Gore collected the best documentary Oscar for his film on global warming, An Inconvenient Truth.
2007-04-25: Apple's independent directors, including Al Gore, publicly expressed complete confidence in Steve Jobs amid a stock options scandal.
2007-06-22: Al Gore spoke at the Cannes advertising festival about the ad industry's role in tackling climate change and received the first-ever "green" Cannes Advertising Festival award.
2007-06-28: A New Hampshire poll suggests Democratic voters would prefer former Vice-President Al Gore over declared 2008 contenders, though Gore has repeatedly denied planning a White House run.
2007-06-29: A poll suggests Democratic voters would prefer former Vice President Al Gore to declared contenders including Hillary Clinton, though Gore has repeatedly denied planning a White House run.

2007-08-15: Al Gore's Current TV hires MTV Networks Europe's David Ridings as its first marketing director for the UK and Ireland operation.
2007-09-06: Former US vice-president Al Gore is working on a new environmental book, The Path to Survival, a sequel to An Inconvenient Truth, planned for publication in spring 2008.

2007-10-11: Al Gore and the UN climate change panel share the 2007 Nobel peace prize for raising awareness of the risks of climate change.
2007-10-12: Al Gore wins Nobel Peace Prize.

2007-10-14: A High Court ruling required Al Gore's climate change documentary to be screened in secondary schools with guidance notes to balance its claims, following a challenge by a school governor supported by a network of business interests linked to fuel and mining lobbies.
2007-10-15: Al Gore is rumoured to be considering a last-minute bid to be the Democratic party's presidential candidate.
2007-10-17: Al Gore was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for alerting the world to the dangers of man-made climate change.
Al Gore said he had no plans to run for the White House despite winning the Nobel peace prize.
2007-10-18: Al Gore rules out running as a candidate in the 2008 presidential elections, saying he has no plans to be a candidate again and is instead focused on a global campaign to address the climate crisis.
2008-01-28: Al Gore's interactive television company Current Media plans to float on the Nasdaq stock market to pay off $36.5m in debts.
2008-02-16: Al Gore emerges as a potential power broker and possible mediator in the Democratic nomination battle between Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama, while remaining neutral.
2008-03-04: Apple shareholders approved a proposal for a regular vote on executive remuneration despite opposition from Steve Jobs and boardroom colleagues including Al Gore.
2008-03-30: Al Gore unveils a $300 million advertising campaign intended to force a debate on climate change during the presidential elections.
2008-03-31: Al Gore announced he would run again for president of the United States, and in November he won the White House in a landslide.

2008-06-16: Al Gore endorses Barack Obama for president and vows to do whatever he can to ensure Obama is elected.
2008-07-17: Former Vice President Al Gore asked the American people to join an ambitious plan to source 100% of American electricity from "clean and truly renewable" sources in 10 years.

2008-11-07: Al Gore urges the US to set a goal of moving to 100% renewable energy within 10 years, calling on Barack Obama to make it one of his first acts as president.
2008-12-12: Al Gore calls for a tougher global carbon dioxide limit of 350 parts per million at UN climate talks in Poznan, Poland.

2009-03-14: Al Gore says in a newspaper interview that a political tipping point has been reached and he believes a global climate deal will be agreed at the UN climate talks in Copenhagen in December.

2009-11-03: Al Gore's new book launch prompts questions about whether his investments in green technology amount to a conflict of interest.

2017-08-16: A review is published of "An Inconvenient Sequel," a documentary following Al Gore through 2015 and 2016 as he addresses climate change and the Climate Reality Leadership Corps program.
2017-08-20: A review is published of "An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power," a documentary featuring Al Gore's climate change advocacy.
